headline: Readiness is climbing back (48, after cratering to 11 Monday) but your fitness read still flags red on load and sleep — trim today's tempo, don't skip the recovery work it's asking for.
body_state: Sleep score 73 (up from 66), but only ~6.3h and a 25h 14-day sleep debt — go to bed ~60min earlier for the next two weeks. HRV balanced at 48ms, body battery recharged +48 overnight, skin temp normal (+0.2°C, no illness signal). Resting HR 50, a touch above your recent 46-48 norm. The deterministic verdict: **band red, driver sleep** — ACWR 1.83 (>1.5 = 2-4x injury risk) and monotony 2.1 (>2.0 overtraining precursor) are both flagged. TSB -14 is still a productive training zone, which is the one green light in the mix.
session: Plan calls for a 4km Tempo Run: 10min easy warmup (4:50-5:19/km) → 4km @ threshold 4:18-4:32/km → 10min easy cooldown. Given the load-spike/sleep-debt flags, trim it — run 2-3km of the tempo rather than the full 4, and if the legs feel flat in the first km, downgrade to a steady effort instead. Target RPE 6-7, not 7-8. This is exactly the "drop one session or trim distances" call your fitness read is making — the goal today is protecting the block, not proving fitness.
recent: Yesterday's 32km bike ride was the pattern you need more of: 70%+ in Zone 1-2, aerobic TE 2.5, zero Zone 4/5 — genuinely easy, no cost. Tuesday's "5km Easy Run" wasn't: 90% of it sat in HR zone 3 at 4:27/km, and cadence is still chronically low at 157.6spm against your 170-180 target. That grey-zone pattern (only 17.8% true easy vs an 80% target) is your #1 ranked limiter. Readiness has climbed steadily since Monday's crash (11 → 52 → 48) — the two easy/impact-free days since then did their job.
focus: Trim today's tempo to 2-3km — protect the load spike (ACWR 1.83), don't extend it
Slow easy days down to HR 115-130 / 5:00+/km — grey-zone training is the #1 limiter
Bank sleep: 25h debt over 14 days — earlier lights-out this week, not just tonight
